summary: Repo-owned coordination layer for the full Steven Woods public suite. Per-project manifests remain the factual status layer; this file is the judgment layer for priority, quality, likely current work, and next-step tradeoffs.
use_this_page_for: Keep one durable portfolio-level mental model in the repo instead of in chat only.
Separate factual project status from portfolio judgment, so the manifest exports can stay factual while priority and time-energy-value tradeoffs can change faster.
Make reprioritization explicit by editing one small source file and rerendering the public and repo-readable overview surfaces.
update_workflow: Update the owning project manifest or archive manifest first when factual project status changes.
Edit this file when priority_now, likely_current_work, next_step, quality_note, or drift_note changes materially.
Run `python3 tools/refresh_public_coordination.py` to validate the suite notes and rerender the repo overview plus homepage from the current manifests.
Use `python3 tools/refresh_public_coordination.py --check` when you want a no-write drift check for the generated coordination surfaces.
tev_rules: Protect already-public software and reference surfaces before starting wide new research lanes.
Prefer publish-refresh work when local archive or documentation progress already exists but the public surface is behind; that is often the best time-energy-value move.
Use small seeding passes for scaffolded archives instead of broad redesigns.
Treat this overview as the place to reprioritize, and the per-project manifests as the place to state factual current status.

priority_bands.label: Protect public surfaces
priority_bands.description: Keep already-public software, docs, and dashboards trustworthy before expanding scope.

priority_bands.label: Publish local progress
priority_bands.description: High-value, usually lower-energy work where repo docs or manifests are already ahead of the public surface.

priority_bands.label: Steady advance
priority_bands.description: Important ongoing work that benefits from regular small batches rather than a one-off push.

priority_bands.label: Seed and clarify
priority_bands.description: Early-stage areas where a small baseline is more valuable than broad exploration.

priority_bands.label: Private tracking
priority_bands.description: Keep only a high-level public summary while the underlying work remains private.

aurora-galactica.likely_current_work: Post-release follow-through on the Aurora and Platinum public family, including lane trust, Galaxy Guardians readiness, and cleaner platform-versus-application seams.
aurora-galactica.next_step: Do a quick Aurora release-lane status refresh before any shared-public publish so the manifest and the active release lane stay aligned.
aurora-galactica.quality_note: This is the strongest product-style public surface in the suite, so small inconsistencies are disproportionately expensive.
aurora-galactica.drift_note: Aurora publishes from a separate repo on a faster cadence than this shared hub, so verify the exported manifest before broad public-repo refreshes.
aurora-galactica.coordination_note: Best handled as protect-and-verify work rather than broad redesign.

confidential-project.likely_current_work: Private rental-portal delivery and related product execution.
confidential-project.next_step: Keep the public summary minimal and accurate; do not expand the public surface unless there is a deliberate client-safe artifact to add.
confidential-project.quality_note: The public/private boundary is already clear, which is the main quality goal here.
confidential-project.coordination_note: Track only high-level continuity in public.

ai-dystopia-quotes.likely_current_work: Ongoing corpus expansion, stronger discovery lanes, and continued approval-quality curation rather than platform work.
ai-dystopia-quotes.next_step: Keep adding high-quality approved entries in batches and refresh the public export whenever the approved corpus meaningfully grows.
ai-dystopia-quotes.quality_note: The public page already reads cleanly and feels complete enough to trust; the main question is breadth and selection quality.
ai-dystopia-quotes.coordination_note: A good example of a healthy incremental export loop.

phd-renovation.likely_current_work: Disciplined intake, continuity hardening, and bounded 1.x cleanup around the stable 1.0.0 baseline.
phd-renovation.next_step: Continue intake and warning cleanup without destabilizing the verified baseline, then refresh the handbook and dashboard only when the supported story changes materially.
phd-renovation.quality_note: One of the most mature documentation and validation surfaces in the suite.
phd-renovation.coordination_note: Good candidate for steady, bounded progress rather than urgent intervention.

mmath-renovation.likely_current_work: Portability hardening, handoff clarity, and careful continuation from the 1.0.0-rc.1 restoration baseline.
mmath-renovation.next_step: Keep the release-candidate surface trustworthy, then only widen into deeper benchmark or hosted-runner work once the portability story is comfortably stable.

mmath-renovation.coordination_note: Treat the hosted runner as mechanism, not the project identity.

steven-woods-research.likely_current_work: Person-centric continuity work, baseline identity tightening, profile preservation, and keeping the source-manifest and review-ledger split deliberate.
steven-woods-research.next_step: Preserve the remaining URL-backed baseline pages and reconcile the review-ledger-only captures that should become formal source records.
steven-woods-research.quality_note: One of the best organized archive areas, with clear role boundaries and strong continuity surfaces.
steven-woods-research.coordination_note: Use this as the canonical person-centric layer, not a dumping ground for company-depth material.

google-canada-research.next_step: Add one more interview or ecosystem source batch, then tighten the public summary only if the center of gravity changes materially.
google-canada-research.quality_note: Now has a seeded, continuity-safe public baseline with room for deeper source density.
google-canada-research.coordination_note: Good candidate for steady, source-batch progress rather than another structural pass.

inovia-research.likely_current_work: Seeded-baseline maintenance plus current-role, team-profile, and ecosystem appearance capture.
inovia-research.next_step: Localize the current team profile and add one more public-appearance or ecosystem source batch.
inovia-research.quality_note: The continuity structure is in place; the main gap now is source depth rather than project setup.
inovia-research.coordination_note: Best advanced through small, explicit source batches.

canberra-research.next_step: Seed the first CSIRO, Canberra Knights, and local-context sources so the archive has a real evidence floor.

sei-pittsburgh-research.likely_current_work: Seeded-baseline maintenance plus additional staff, paper, and startup-transition context around the SEI-to-Quack bridge.
sei-pittsburgh-research.next_step: Add one more staff or transition-context batch, then refresh the summary only when the bridge story materially improves.

sei-pittsburgh-research.coordination_note: Good steady research lane now that the scaffold phase is over.

quack-com.likely_current_work: Preservation and source-completeness work around AOL by Phone, investor outcomes, first-party capture gaps, and stronger preserved press.
quack-com.next_step: Keep working campaign-by-campaign, preserving fragile or first-party evidence before widening the editorial surface.

quack-com.coordination_note: Treat the bridge record as compatibility, not as a second canonical home.

kinitos-neoedge.likely_current_work: A pushed Kinitos branch has finished the approved-source preservation floor and added private-evidence derivative notes, even though the public line still understates that progress.
kinitos-neoedge.next_step: Promote the preservation-complete Kinitos branch, then shift into deferred-source and public-corroboration follow-up instead of more blocked-press preservation.
